newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil holds, Singapore fall fails to impact.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil holds, Singapore fall fails to impact.

text.p: NWE gas oil was slightly softer as futures eased, but premiums held steady despite tumbling Singapore prices.
July IPE gas oil, which expires on Thursday, was trading at $162.50 at 1100 GMT, only 25 cents off the open.
Dealers said prompt barges were tight and attracting keen prices. A trade was concluded at $1.50, but as yet interest for second half material was flagging.
"When people start talking about second half it will be against August," said one dealer.

There was little consensus about the possible impact of the sharp fall in Singapore prices where gas oil lost about $1 a barrel. Swaps collapsed on Wednesday in Singapore after a massive selloff triggerd by oil majors selling on weak regional fundamentals and easier crude.
Some traders thought European levels would have to dip in response, while others said it was too early to tell.
Diesel barges were pegged around July IPE +$5.00 fob, while cargoes were being offered as low as July +$3.50.
